item.title: Odoo Toolbox
item.description: Odoo ERP integration for AI agents
item.content:encoded:
AI-friendly Odoo integration — progressive knowledge modules and TypeScript client for working with Odoo v17 ERP.

What It Does

Teaches AI agents how to work with Odoo through progressive, CI-tested skill modules. Instead of dumping 12,000 pages of Odoo docs into context, agents load only what they need: connection → domains → CRUD → domain-specific (mail, accounting, timesheets).

Every code example in the skills is extracted and tested against a real Odoo v17 instance in CI. No doc rot, no hallucinated APIs.

Quick Start

Install (updated 2026-02-15)

npx skills add marcfargas/odoo-toolbox

TypeScript packages:

npm install @marcfargas/odoo-client
npm install @marcfargas/odoo-introspection

Scaffold a skill project:

npx @marcfargas/create-odoo-skills my-odoo-skills

What’s Inside

(Check repository for up to date list of skills)

  • 8 foundational skills: connection, domains, field types, CRUD, search, introspection, properties, modules
  • 5 domain-specific skills: mail/chatter, accounting, contracts, attendance, timesheets
  • TypeScript client: Lightweight RPC client (@marcfargas/odoo-client)
  • Schema introspection: Discover models/fields dynamically (@marcfargas/odoo-introspection)
  • All skills CC0 (public domain) — code is LGPL-3.0

Repository · npm packages

item.title: Go Easy
item.content:encoded:
Unified TypeScript library and CLIs for Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and Tasks — designed for AI agents.

What It Does

Wraps Google’s official APIs in a single library with four agent-friendly CLIs:

  • go-gmail: Read, search, send email; manage drafts; handle threads
  • go-drive: Upload, download, search files; manage folders
  • go-calendar: Create events, manage calendars, query availability
  • go-tasks: Create, update, list tasks across task lists

Two-phase OAuth works in headless environments (auth in browser, token to server). Pagination, encoding quirks, and token refresh handled transparently.

Quick Start

Skills list unavailable at build time. See repository for current skills.

Install CLIs:

npm install -g @marcfargas/go-easy

TypeScript library:

npm install @marcfargas/go-easy

First-time auth (interactive):

npx go-gmail auth

Then agents can call:

npx go-gmail search "from:john subject:invoice"
npx go-drive upload report.pdf --folder-id <id>
npx go-calendar create "Team sync" --start "2026-02-20T10:00:00"
npx go-tasks create "Review proposal" --list-id <id>

What’s Inside

  • 4 gateway CLIs: go-gmail, go-drive, go-calendar, go-tasks
  • TypeScript library: @marcfargas/go-easy (also exports programmatic API)
  • AI Agent Skill: Teaches agents the CLI patterns, auth flow, common operations
  • Skills CC0 (public domain) — code is MIT

Repository · npm

item.title: Go MAPI
item.content:encoded:
Open-source MAPI-to-Gmail bridge for Windows — makes “Send by Email” work with Gmail.

What It Does

Intercepts MAPI calls (Windows’ “Send by Email” API) and creates Gmail drafts via browser extension. Right-click a file in Explorer → Send → Gmail draft opens with file attached.

Every Windows app that can email uses MAPI: PDF printers, accounting software, scanners, CRMs. Gmail has no native MAPI support. The only third-party solution (Affixa) shut down. Go MAPI is the open-source replacement.

Handles ANSI/Unicode, multiple attachments, and codepage encoding edge cases that enterprise Windows software produces.

Install

Extension (required):
Chrome Web Store · Edge Add-ons

Native host (Windows):

iwr https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marcfargas/go-mapi/main/install.ps1 | iex

After install, “Send by Email” will create Gmail drafts instead of opening Outlook/Mail.

Architecture

Windows app → MAPI call → Native host (Rust) → Chrome extension → Gmail draft (via Google APIs)

Repository · Install guide

item.title: Skills
item.description: Reusable skills for AI coding agents
item.content:encoded:
Agent-agnostic skills that teach AI agents how to use specific tools — structured markdown “man pages” for LLMs.

What It Is

Skills are standalone markdown files that tell an agent:

  • How to operate a CLI
  • What’s safe to run (safety classification)
  • What patterns to follow
  • What gotchas to avoid

CC0-licensed (public domain). Works with pi, Claude Code, Cursor, and any agent that reads markdown.

Available Skills

Skills list unavailable at build time. See repository for current skills.

Skill Breakdown

Cloud & Infrastructure

  • azcli — Azure CLI (az) for managing Azure resources
  • gcloud — Google Cloud Platform CLI (gcloud, gcloud storage, bq)

Development & Release

  • pm2 — Process management (start, stop, restart, monitor)
  • pre-release — Pre-release review and changeset generation
  • repo-hygiene — Repository health checks
  • vhs — Terminal recording as GIF/MP4/WebM

Search & Discovery

  • web-search — Web search via ddgs (multi-engine metasearch)

Data & Modeling

  • sheet-model — Headless spreadsheet engine for financial models

Install

List available skills:

npx skills add marcfargas/skills --list

Install a specific skill:

npx skills add marcfargas/skills --skill azcli
npx skills add marcfargas/skills --skill gcloud
npx skills add marcfargas/skills --skill pm2
npx skills add marcfargas/skills --skill sheet-model

Install all skills:

npx skills add marcfargas/skills --skill '*'

Interactive install (prompts if multiple skills available):

npx skills add marcfargas/skills

From source:

git clone https://github.com/marcfargas/skills
# Point your agent at skills/<name>/SKILL.md

Pattern

The motivation: every time an agent struggles with a CLI, the fix is better instructions. Skills make those instructions reusable across projects and agents.

Emerged from odoo-toolbox and go-easy (both ship skills). Generalized into a standalone collection.

Repository · skills.sh registry

item.title: Holdpty
item.content:encoded:
Launch commands in a real pseudo-terminal, detach, reattach later. Cross-platform screen / tmux alternative for AI agents.

What It Does

Creates detached PTY sessions that survive disconnection. Windows (named pipes), macOS, and Linux (Unix sockets). Agents can launch long-running processes, detach, and check back later without blocking.

Supports logs --tail/--follow, session replay, Ctrl+A detach in attached mode, and PowerShell compatibility.

Quick Start

Install (updated 2026-02-15)

npx skills add marcfargas/holdpty

Install CLI:

npm install -g holdpty

Usage:

holdpty launch my-session -- npm run dev
holdpty logs my-session --follow
holdpty attach my-session
holdpty list

Repository · npm

item.title: Pi Planner
item.content:encoded:
Structured plan-then-execute workflow for pi agents — review multi-step operations as a unit before execution.

What It Does

When an agent needs to touch external systems (Odoo, email, calendar, deployments), it proposes the full sequence first. You review the plan as a unit, approve once, and the agent executes.

Prevents the “confirm each tool call individually” problem. You can’t assess a 5-step workflow one click at a time.

Features

  • Plan mode: Restricts tools to read-only during planning
  • Skill safety registry: Classifies bash commands as READ or WRITE
  • Persistent plans: Markdown files in .pi/plans/ (auditable, diffable, survive crashes)
  • Crash recovery: Resumes stalled plans from checkpoints
  • Model override: Execute plans with a specific model (e.g., faster/cheaper for known-good plans)

Install

npm install @marcfargas/pi-planner

Add to pi config (~/.pi/extensions/):

{
  "extensions": ["npm:@marcfargas/pi-planner"]
}

Part of the pi-mf-extensions monorepo.

Repository · npm

item.title: Pi Safety
item.description: Safety classification registry for AI agent tool calls
item.content:encoded:
A library that classifies AI agent tool calls as READ (no side effects) or WRITE (everything else) using glob-based command pattern matching.

When an AI agent runs npx go-gmail marc@example.com search "invoice", that’s a read. When it runs npx go-gmail marc@example.com send --to bob@example.com, that’s a write. Pi Safety provides the registry where skills declare their safety levels, and downstream tools (like Pi Planner) enforce them.

Patterns use glob wildcards and are registered per tool/CLI. The LLM itself acts as the parser — when it loads a skill, it extracts the safety classifications and registers them. This means any new skill automatically gets safety enforcement without manual configuration.

Part of the pi-mf-extensions monorepo.

item.title: Pi Test Harness
item.content:encoded:
Test framework for pi extensions — verify extension behavior without running a full LLM session.

What It Does

Pi extensions add tool calls to agents, but testing is awkward: you’d need to spin up a model, craft prompts that trigger tools, and parse output.

Pi Test Harness provides a mock pi environment where you can:

  • Call extension tools directly
  • Assert on outputs
  • Verify state changes
  • Test tool interactions

Playbook-based: write scenarios in YAML, run with real pi runtime (extensions, tools, hooks), model mocked via streamFn.

Install

npm install --save-dev @marcfargas/pi-test-harness

Example

import { runPlaybook } from '@marcfargas/pi-test-harness';

const result = await runPlaybook('./test-plan-lifecycle.yml', {
  extensions: ['npm:@marcfargas/pi-planner'],
});

expect(result.status).toBe('success');

Used to test pi-planner’s plan lifecycle, pi-safety’s glob matching, and plan mode tool restrictions.

Part of the pi-mf-extensions monorepo.

Repository · npm

item.title: Pi Server
item.content:encoded:
Run pi as a headless daemon, connect and disconnect terminal clients at will — your session keeps running.

Pi is a powerful coding agent, but it’s tied to your terminal. Close the tab, lose the session. Pi Server fixes that: it wraps pi in a WebSocket-accessible daemon. Connect your terminal, work with the agent, disconnect, reconnect later and pick up where you left off.

The foundation for remote agent access — run pi on a powerful server, connect from a laptop. Also the building block for web dashboards, mobile clients, and multi-agent orchestration where sessions need to outlive any single connection.

Alpha status. Under active development.

item.title: django-mailserver
item.content:encoded:
A Django application for creating mail services — virtual domains, mailboxes, and aliases managed through Django’s admin interface, backed by Postfix and Dovecot.

Built in 2009, when self-hosted email was how you ran a business. 16 stars on GitHub — modest, but it solved a real problem for a few people running their own mail infrastructure on Django.

Archived. A relic from a time when “cloud email” meant your own VPS with Postfix.

item.title: importaSOL
item.content:encoded:
Librería Python para generar archivos XLS importables en las aplicaciones ContaSOL, GestorSOL, NominaSOL y demás productos del ecosistema SOL (Sage España).

Nació de la necesidad de migrar datos contables entre sistemas — cuando tienes cientos de asientos y la única vía de entrada es un formato Excel propietario, automatizarlo no es opcional.

Archivado. El ecosistema SOL sigue existiendo, pero los flujos de datos han cambiado.

item.title: SignalFlow
item.content:encoded:
A Python library for signal-based flow programming — connect processing nodes with typed signals, build reactive data pipelines declaratively.

An experiment in making data flow explicit: instead of calling functions, you connect signals. A node emits, downstream nodes react. The idea predates the current wave of “AI agent pipelines” by several years, though the motivation was different — real-time data processing, not LLM orchestration.

Archived. The concept was sound; the timing was early.
